correctness.rationale: Rechecked exact quantified clauses in Kaminski 2026 Definition 2 against package M1/M2. M1 makes active worlds a suffix and outputs an increasing chain in product order. M2 at last world forces (N,N). If both coordinates below N at first active world, M2 demands incomparable (a+1,b) and (a,b+1) among that monotone output chain, impossible: one coordinate must equal N for all active rows. M2 then forces every integer between initial free coordinate and N to occur, equivalent to unit-or-zero increments. Conversely all such normal forms satisfy each M1/M2 quantifier. For suffix length m, 2^m−1 options from two orientations minus constant duplicate; sum yields formula. Independently exhaustively checked all partial functions for n=1,2,3,4 and commutative/total subcases; no extrapolation from computation.
residual_risks: Finite checks only corroborate, not replace the all-parameter proof.

final_claim: For n>=1, all ternary relations on a labelled n-world chain with at most one ordered output pair per world satisfying Kaminski monotonicity (M1),(M2) are empty or a suffix of active worlds with a single output coordinate fixed at the top and the other moving by increments 0 or 1 to the top. Counts: 2^(n+1)−n−1 partial-functional, 2^n−1 total-functional, n+1 target-symmetric partial.
